Cleaning width depends on the task: 450 mm for sweeping/vacuuming and 285 mm for scrubbing; machine mass includes the battery and empty water tanks.
Separate 7 L clean-water and 5 L wastewater tanks avoid reusing dirty water; tank volume is not rated cargo payload.
Removable sweeping/vacuum, dust-bin, rear-mop and side-brush modules support maintenance. App/web tools cover remote dispatch, status and cleaning reports.

highlights: The manufacturer explicitly names Blaze with 1550 mm including MIG torch. Standard Blaze and long-reach Max are separate named sizes; neither reach is a bare-arm radius without the torch.

The page lists up to 2540 mm/min welding feed, continuous/tack/stitch/weave modes and ±0.1 mm repeatability. Feed is process motion, not a free-motion TCP limit; repeatability is not absolute positioning accuracy or a guaranteed weld-quality result.

Teach-by-touch, drag-and-drop recipes and compatibility with Miller, Lincoln and other welders support integration. Miller Auto-Continuum and Auto Deltaweld 350/500 are selectable source options; amperage, power and source duty cycle are not robot payload or runtime.

An optional synchronized rotary positioning table adds an external axis. The cobot remains seven-axis; the table is not an additional robot. IP61 is stated for the sealed controller and IP41 for the tablet on this page, without certifying a complete MIG installation rating.

The laser page explicitly separates Blaze Laser at 1550 mm including laser torch. The series page calls the larger version Blaze Max Laser; this is the same linked larger-size offering, not a third laser-arm card.

The linked two-size PDF gives up to 2540 mm/min welding feed and ±0.1 mm repeatability. It separately gives 2 m/s maximum position-dependent linear motion and a 0-2+ m/s speed line; the motion-speed discrepancy stays qualified. Feed, free motion and repeatability remain different metrics.

The robot specification states IP61, alongside a separately rated IP61 sealed controller and IP41 tablet. A shared 22 kg/58 lb robot mass is internally inconsistent and not assigned to either size; Miller source mass 64 kg is not the whole robot or cell.

Miller OptX 1 kW is listed for welding; 2 kW adds cleaning. The 2 kW PDF lists 32 A input while LF/Mobile option tables list 20 A; the exact selected-source revision needs confirmation, not a unified electrical requirement. The PDF distinguishes a Class 4 processing laser and Class 2M guide beam.

Marketing about doubled productivity, any-material welding or no safety equipment is not independently certified. Laser power, source duty cycle and cleaning width are not battery endurance or robot payload.

highlights: Six base T200 thrusters provide vectored underwater movement. The optional Heavy kit adds two vertical thrusters and full six-axis vehicle control with pitch/roll stabilization; it does not increase horizontal speed.
Acrylic and aluminum tubes retain separate 100 m and 300 m depth ratings. The listed 457 × 338 × 254 mm base envelope is distinct from extended skids and tether lengths.

Mass is 11–12 kg with default ballast and manufacturer battery, or 9–10 kg without either. Available buoyancy is 1.2 kg with four Lumen lights to 1.4 kg with none; the 7 kgf vertical thrust is not neutral carried payload.

Both active sources state roughly two-hour normal/four-hour light operation, but the HTML table specifies 15.6 Ah and its linked PDF 18 Ah. The battery-condition mismatch remains unresolved instead of becoming an unconditional maximum.

Navigator and BlueOS support configurable control and sensing. A tilting 1080p camera is described; extra sonars, grippers and payload skids remain optional integrations rather than assumed stock autonomous inspection capabilities.

The visible price starts at 4,900 USD with tax excluded. The buyer guide says the base package excludes tether and lights; battery, charger and laptop also need to be supplied. Kit assembly is estimated at six to eight hours.

A roughly thirty-second battery exchange is not charging duration. The selected sources do not establish a whole-vehicle IP code, exact charge interval, first-release year or independently verified task outcome.

highlights: The 14.5 kg vehicle mass excludes batteries and instruments; the 15 kg allowance combines batteries with payload. The 3 m/s maximum uses two batteries with no payload, rather than a fully loaded survey configuration.

At 1 m/s and about 30 W without payload, the table lists 18/36/50/62 hours for two/four/six/eight batteries. The largest setup is 2,128 Wh; optional solar indefinite operation is not battery-only endurance.
Twin M200 motors and weedless propellers steer through differential thrust. Overall table dimensions are 120 × 93 × 46 cm deployed and 120 × 71 × 24 cm folded; packaging dimensions remain separate.

GPS, Navigator, ArduRover and BlueOS support manual, waypoint, guided and position-hold operation. The operator guide defaults non-Auto telemetry loss to motor-stopping Hold, while Auto ignores that failsafe; return-home behavior depends on configuration.

Standard-antenna telemetry/control is listed up to 250 m; optional directional antennas exceed 800 m under suitable conditions. Communication reach is not sonar survey depth, guaranteed mission range or collision avoidance.

The manufacturer starting price is 4,400 USD before tax. Batteries, charger, computer and selected sonar/radio accessories need the appropriate supplied-system configuration; the starting vehicle price is not a complete survey package.

Payload interfaces and BlueOS support integrating survey instruments, cameras and communications. Optional sonar accuracy, a BaseStation charge indication and 320 mm maximum loaded draft are not vehicle navigation accuracy, vehicle charge duration or a diving-depth rating.

Die-cast aluminum body, acrylic window and magnetically coupled/sealed drives. The camera specification describes enhanced 4K video, 8 MP stills and 270° total range of view; this is not an extra body degree of freedom.

Six independently controlled, fully reversible thrusters and 19.2 VDC power. The page specifies enhanced 4K video and 8 MP stills. The tether can be up to 300 m; tether length is not the 120 m depth rating.

Six independently controlled, fully reversible thrusters and 19.2 VDC power. Enhanced 4K video and 8 MP stills are specified. USBL, DVL and sonar support depends on package and add-ons; no universal numeric positioning tolerance is established.

The embedded FAQ describes a 97° tilting shelf separately from 220° camera rotation. Accessories and imaging angles are not arm joint counts or guaranteed positioning accuracy.

The named REVOLUTION specification lists 33 kg in air, 717 x 440 x 235 mm body dimensions in length × width × height order, and 305 m depth rating. Cases, controllers, tether reels and tool assemblies are separate.

The electrical specification lists 19.2 VDC, 18 Ah LiFePO4. Copper tether options up to 300 m and fiber options up to 2 km are not dive-depth or battery-runtime figures. Enhanced 4K video and 8 MP stills are specified.

No exact per-charge endurance, full-charge duration, payload, complete-robot IP class or first hardware-release year is established by this reviewed product page. Portable power and batteries do not supply numeric endurance by inference.

The named SPECTRA specification lists 38 kg in air, 790 x 586 x 296 mm body dimensions in length × width × height order, and 1000 m depth rating. Cases, controllers, tether reels and tool assemblies are separate.
Seven thrusters comprise four vectored and three vertical units. The stated 40 kg thrust force is not payload. Dual 4K video and 12 MP stills accompany two 150,000-lumen lights, 300,000 lumens total.

Visible specifications list 3.5 knots forward and 2.3 knots lateral, but embedded Product JSON-LD describes 4 knots maximum. The source conflict remains explicit. Maximum current-operation wording is not an independently tested capability.

Real-time Sonar SLAM is explicitly enabled with 3D sonar only. The 300 m standard fiber tether and additional kilometer options are separate from the 1000 m depth rating; sonar integration is not universally included.

Direct topside power is specified at 100–260 VAC, 50–60 Hz and 7200 W maximum draw, with 48 V nominal onboard and 1000 W accessory-port power. Accessory watts are not payload. Under-30-minute modular servicing is not a charge time or battery duration.

MAG uses magnetic wheels on ferrous surfaces, magnetically coupled final drives and a 19.2 V lithium battery system. The product page advertises enhanced 4K cameras and sonar integration; tooling and sonar configuration require confirmation.

The general specification gives 16.6 kg, 710 mm length, 406 mm width and 228 mm height, with 50 m depth rating. Width is also labeled 13 inches, inconsistent with 406 mm; the source disagreement is retained.
The page labels 360° as turn radius. An angle is not a length, so no numeric turning radius or zero-clearance guarantee is selected.

The IP68 claim is under Tether Reel, not the robot. The 150 kg minimum tether breaking strength is not crawler payload. Tether options of 50–400 m and the standard 75 m reel are distinct from 50 m dive depth.
Incline, roll, leak and camera-pan/tilt sensors do not establish numeric navigation accuracy. Exact battery endurance and full-charge duration are not documented on the reviewed page.
The VAC family page lists 15 kg, 710 × 406 × 228 mm, 50 m submersion depth, 12 m/min speed and rubber 2WD. It pairs 406 mm width with 13 inches; that unresolved unit conflict remains visible.

The shop package states up to eight hours on battery and hybrid trickle charging during operation. This is not a full-charge duration, nor a guarantee for maximum speed, cleaning load or indefinite battery-only operation.

The two-inch vacuum intakes connect to a hose and submersible pump. The shop explicitly excludes the hose and pump. The articulated head has separate 20° raise and tilt travel, which is not a manipulator joint count.

Camera revision is unresolved: the visible family specification says enhanced 4K, while the shop embedded electrical table says 1080p main-camera video with 8 MP sensor data. Neither image pixels nor the family headline reconcile the delivered video mode.

The stated zero-millimeter turning radius does not establish zero surrounding clearance. IP68 belongs to the tether reel, and 150 kg tether strength is not crawler payload. The shop URL containing XL and 18-inch is not evidence of a separate VAC XL model.
